exposure: Pre-pregnancy Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) (chronic hypertension, pre-gestational diabetes, cardiac disease, chronic kidney disease, sickle cell disease, asthma, epilepsy)
Inadequate antenatal care (fewer than four ANC visits)
outcome: Severe maternal outcomes (maternal death, acute heart failure, ICU admission, pulmonary embolism, sepsis)
Adverse perinatal outcomes (miscarriage, neonatal death, NICU admission)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 300 pregnant women (100 with NCDs and 200 without NCDs) admitted to the maternity ward of Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital.
finding: Pre-pregnancy NCDs and inadequate antenatal care (fewer than four visits) were significantly associated with an increased risk of both severe maternal and adverse perinatal outcomes.
